oneLine: A number that shows lenders how well you repaid money before.
explanation: A credit score is a number based on your borrowing history.
A higher score means lenders see less risk. It goes up when you repay on time.
It goes down when you pay late or use too much of your credit limit.
whyItMatters: A good score can give you a lower APR. Over many years, a lower APR can save you a lot of money.
workedExample: Two people borrow $20,000 for a car, for 5 years. One gets a 6% APR. The other gets 12%. The second person pays about $3,500 more in interest.

inTheUs.text: Many scores go from 300 to 850. You can see your credit report for free.
